description:
[EPIC] Dissolve the seal's runtime-demand fixpoint into per-executable facts so demand re-derivation has minimal blast radius, matching the North Star's "one fixpoint loop" instead of a monolithic pass re-run on every increment of discovery.

## Goal
`SealSemanticClosure` is the point where compiler2 stops being incremental. Behind it, `settle_runtime_demands` (jobs/runtime_demand.rs:45) runs a backward-dataflow fixpoint over the WHOLE executable set, re-cloning every analysis and body on every wake. Measured on enum_take_drop_split (411 executables): the seal runs 538 times and changes nothing 535 of them (99.4%); downstream facts bump their revision after first appearance only 3 times in the whole compile. The work is not churn — it is the same monolith re-run on every increment of monotone discovery.

Runtime demand is the exact backward dual of activation inputs. Forward inputs were built correctly as a contribution-joined fact that settles in the drive agenda ("the joined activation fact is the loop"). This epic gives the backward dual the same treatment: per-executable `ReturnDemand` (contribution-joined) and `RuntimeDemand` (derived) facts, so the inner nested fixpoint dissolves into the one agenda and re-derivation touches only the lattice neighborhood that moved.

## Strategy — strangler, not rewrite
`SemanticClosed(root)` is a BARRIER. Keep it byte-identical and nothing downstream can tell the difference. Stand the incremental path up BEHIND the barrier, prove it equals the monolith via a runtime assert in shadow mode, then cut over and delete the monolith. Later passes (transport, materialize) re-point onto these finer facts before we carve fields off the barrier — that is future work; this epic does runtime demand only. See proposal.html for the worked proof (quicksort oracle) and the lfp(F) monotonicity argument.

## Why this is low-risk / correct-by-construction
- The demand lattice is already a documented join-semilattice (semantic.rs:159-231): ShapeDemand x CallableDemand, with join/join_assign and the monotonicity rationale in-code. We invent no lattice.
- `ReturnDemand` is the third member of the existing cumulative-fact club (ClaimShape::is_cumulative, drive.rs:88) alongside ReturnType and ActivationInputs. `ActivationInputMap` (semantic.rs) is the proven template to mirror.
- The transfer functions (derive_executable_runtime_demand, collect_executable_facts, derive_callable_flow_facts) are pure over (facts, demands map); each has exactly one caller. They MOVE verbatim — the per-executable job assembles a small local demands map from neighbor facts and passes it in. Only orchestration changes.
- The shadow assert (assert_eq! gathered-map == settle_runtime_demands output, all six ExecutableRuntimeDemand fields incl. callable_flows) turns the "byte-identical" proof obligation into a runtime invariant exercised corpus-wide BEFORE any deletion. The awkward middle is verified coexistence, not a blind cutover.

## Signal
Seal runs collapse from O(discovery-steps) to ~constant; DeriveRuntimeDemand(E) re-runs only when a neighbor demand ascends; no whole-closure clone per wake; `closure.runtime_demands` and the latent-executable set stay byte-identical (pinned by compiler2_ summary tests + tests/fixture_matrix.rs goldens). The return-widening corpus sweep is untouched — we never go near the type fixpoint.
title: Compiler2 incremental runtime demand: dissolve the seal's demand fixpoint into per-executable facts
